title: Mortality Rate and Serious Complications amongst Singaporeans who Suffer COVID-19 Reinfections
what_it_is: Mortality Rate and Serious Complications amongst Singaporeans who Suffer COVID-19 Reinfections

sections.label: Reinfection mortality and vaccination protection
sections.summary: Reinfection cases had lower mortality and severe illness rates than first infections, and minimum vaccination protection lowered severe illness risk.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: In fact, from September to mid-November 2022, the mortality rate of reinfection cases in Singapore was four per 100,000 cases, lower than that for first-time infection cases at 35 per 100,000 cases.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The rate of severe illness – those requiring oxygen supplementation, intensive care or death – was also lower for reinfections at 232 per 100,000 cases, compared to first-time infections at 282 per 100,000 cases.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Our data also shows that achieving minimum vaccination protection – in other words, three doses of mRNA or four doses of Sinovac – lowers the risk of severe illness, whether it is a first infection or re-infection.

sections.label: Bivalent vaccine effectiveness and vaccination uptake
sections.summary: Bivalent vaccines reduce severe illness, unvaccinated are more likely to fall severely ill, and mobile teams will improve access.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The initial data from clinical trials of the bivalent vaccine and now, empirical data based on our actual lived experience, show that it has been effective in reducing severe illnesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Today, when you compare, especially for the aged, those who have gotten full protection and up-to-date vaccination, versus those who have not, it still shows a significant difference between the prevalence of severe illness if they get infected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: I do not have the data with me, but it is at least four to five times more likely to fall severely ill if you are not fully vaccinated or not update-to-date with the vaccination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Today, we are administering healthy numbers of vaccines – about 20,000 a day in uptake; it is quite good.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We will continue to put out public messages to encourage people to take their vaccine, keep it up-to-date, because the pandemic is not over.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We will be stepping up our mobile vaccination teams into the heartlands so that, especially for the seniors, they will find that it is more accessible to getting their vaccination up-to-date with the mobile vaccination teams in place.

sections.label: Protection rate of vaccines
sections.summary: The protection rate is about 70-plus percent, while mRNA is more effective at 80-plus, almost 90%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: I remember the protection rate is about 70-plus percent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: But if you use mRNA, it is even more effective, at 80-plus, almost 90%.
